assertions.description: navigator.bluetooth is the entry point every part of this feature hangs off.
BluetoothRemoteGATTServer is exposed as a global interface, which is where the new property lives.

maxWriteWithoutResponseSize is exposed on BluetoothRemoteGATTServer.prototype. Feature detection must use the prototype: a disconnected server legitimately has no value, so testing an instance proves nothing.
The property is a readonly accessor on the prototype, not a data property copied onto each instance, so it reflects the live connection state rather than a value captured at connect time.
writeValueWithoutResponse is the operation the size limit applies to.
BluetoothRemoteGATTServer inherits from EventTarget, which is what makes the maxwritewithoutresponsesizechanged event listenable on the server object.
navigator.bluetooth.getAvailability() reports whether an adapter exists without opening the device chooser, so a page can degrade honestly before asking the user for anything.
requestDevice() must reject without transient user activation, which is why every demo here puts it behind a button rather than calling it on load.
assertions.test: (async()=>{try{await navigator.bluetooth.requestDevice({acceptAllDevices:true});return false;}catch(e){return e instanceof DOMException||e instanceof TypeError;}})()
